To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the steric gate of UmuC contributes to UV resistance, and that the steric gates of UmuC and DinB are differentially important for lesion bypass and mutagenesis.

the UmuD′/UmuC system of E. coli is hypersensitive to UV irradiation when the steric gate of UmuC is altered and that the hypersensitivity is partially suppressed by a mutation in the replicative DNA pol III proofreading subunit.

mutations of the sterc gate residue of UmuC confer UV hypersensitivity to the host cell and are dominant negative with regard to sensitivity to UV, and that the dominant negative effect of the steric gage variant is partially suppressed by additional mutation in UmuC motifs that are involved in binding of the β clamp, and is completely suppressed by disruption of dnaQ.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the UmuC protein steric gate in the process of DNA damage bypass.
the role of the steric gating mechanism in the Y family polymerases and the implications of the mechanism for the fidelity of lesion bypass and for the fidelity of replicative DNA polymerization.
a new role of the Y family DNA polymerase steric gate residue, which may be involved in a mechanism of lesion discrimination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Y11A variant of E. coli DNA polymerase UmuC is a dominant negative mutant with respect to UV sensitivity, which is suppressed by the proofreading activity of replicative DNA polymerizes, suggesting that UmuC stochastically engages in a futile cycle in the absence of replicative DNA pol III.
the steric gate of Y family polymerases is involved in the recognition of damaged DNA substrates.
the steric gate of UmuC is involved in lesion bypass activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Y family polymerases have a specific steric gate that is required to access the replication fork.
the steric gate is a major determinant of Y-family polymerase substrate specificity.

the UmuD’2C steric gate residue plays a key role in the ability of UmuD’ 2C to access the replication fork, and this is important for the ability of U muC to contribute to UV resistance and UV mutagenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Y11 steric gate residue is critical for the function of the E. coli U muD/ U muC complex and that the UmuD/ U mu C steric gate variants exhibit dominant negative effects on UV sensitivity.
Y family polymerase steric gate residues can have profound effects on cellular sensitivity to DNA damaging agents.
the Y family DNA polymerase steric gate is important for lesion bypass and that this function can be dominant negative.
